scores.evidence: CI never holds prod credentials, every prod change is a Git commit, and rollback is git revert.
scores.rationale: Claims about GitHub Actions OIDC, reusable workflows, Argo CD sync/PreSync hooks, cosign/Kyverno verification, concurrency groups and GitOps semantics are all accurate, including subtle areas like expand/contract and idempotent promotion.

scores.evidence: a shared build-and-deploy platform. Every one of the ~50 services goes from commit to production through the same audited, reversible path.
scores.rationale: Directly answers the sequencing request with explicit, justified exclusions, but omits flaky-test detection/quarantine and automated contract/schema compatibility checks, both implied core needs for a 50-service CI/CD platform.

scores.evidence: deploy-config is the single source of truth, and Argo CD only reads it. Promotions are serialised per service and environment
scores.rationale: Components, data ownership, trust zones and flows are mutually consistent; decisions (digest promotion, no CI cluster creds, two Argo instances) are honored everywhere with no contradictions.

scores.evidence: four spikes check the riskiest unknowns: database migrations, build speed, private network access from CI, and environment config baked into images
scores.rationale: Risky assumptions get time-boxed spikes before commitment, exit criteria are measurable, rollback is drilled and timed, and DORA/drift monitoring continues in production.

scores.evidence: If any of these is wrong, the plan changes in a big way. The questions at the end say how.
scores.rationale: Every load-bearing assumption is tabulated with impact-if-wrong and a verification task/date, targets are labeled as assumptions to confirm, and no invented specifics are stated as fact.

scores.evidence: If a non-reversible schema migration ran, rolling back the image is safe only because of expand/contract
scores.rationale: Covers domain-specific failures — bad prod deploys, failed migrations, GitHub/Actions/Argo outages, template releases breaking 50 repos, workflow injection, duplicate promotions — each with concrete detection and recovery.

scores.evidence: Business-hours support goes through a #platform-help channel with a weekly rotating platform shield engineer.
scores.rationale: Ownership, SLOs, meaningful alerts, tested runbooks, break-glass paths and a support model sized to 4 engineers are designed in, with safe change via fixture repos and staged Renovate rollout.

scores.evidence: about 200k Actions minutes/month at about $0.008–0.016/min comes to about $1.6–3.2k
scores.rationale: Dominant drivers (CI minutes, people time per service) are quantified with stated bases and labeled rough, with concrete controls (cancel superseded runs, lifecycle rules, spend alert) and a managed-vs-self-hosted trade-off.

scores.evidence: Point of no return: deleting the legacy Jenkins jobs and scripts in M4. Gate: 50/50 services onboarded and 2 weeks with no out-of-band prod deploys.
scores.rationale: Every key decision carries an explicit reversibility rating and revisit trigger, hard-to-change items (OIDC/network/GitOps commitment) are validated early, and fallback to old pipelines exists until a gated decommission.

scores.evidence: Building a developer portal (Backstage) or per-PR preview environments. Both are deferred (§17).
scores.rationale: Each component is tied to a stated driver, speculative items are deferred with explicit triggers, and the escape-hatch contract avoids 50 bespoke pipelines without over-standardizing.

scores.evidence: If the review slips past week 4, M1 closes with the pilot in staging and a prod date set. Raise this as the #1 risk.
scores.rationale: Day-1 actions, dependency-ordered tasks with checkable done-when criteria, milestone exit criteria, and explicit adaptations if spikes or reviews disappoint mean a team could start immediately.

checklist.evidence: Inventory all 50 services: repo, language/build tool, current deploy method... Classify each as A... B... C... or D (unusual).
Get it running in dev, then staging, with the old pipeline still deploying prod.
Build once, promote the same digest... No rebuilding per environment.
GitHub OIDC to a cloud role... fork PRs get no secrets... ESO from the secret manager
Actions pinned by SHA... Trivy... SBOM, signatures and Kyverno verification... branch protection plus CODEOWNERS guard envs/prod/
The rule is expand/contract. Each release's migrations must stay compatible with the previous image version.
Owning each team's integration test suites. The platform provides the hook to run them, not the tests.
Per-PR preview environments... deferred... Teams report staging contention as a top-3 complaint
Can PR feedback hit p90 ≤ 10 min for the slowest 3 builds in the inventory on GitHub-hosted runners with caching?
about 200k Actions minutes/month at about $0.008–0.016/min comes to about $1.6–3.2k... ARC self-hosted runners for heavy builds
Platform SLO: 99.5% CI success rate... the four DORA metrics... pages the platform on-call
Prod changes go through a PR with CODEOWNERS set per service folder... Git history, kept indefinitely: this is the audit trail

traps.evidence: Move services in waves, archetype by archetype... the old pipeline stays available until the end.
Build once, promote the same digest... No :latest tag.
CI has no long-lived cloud credentials... fork PRs get no secrets
an Argo CD ApplicationSet... creates one Application per folder... Prod changes go through a PR... per service folder
CI runs on GitHub Actions using central, versioned reusable workflows... Argo CD applies it

note: An exemplary, technically precise plan that avoids every trap, sequences by risk with early spikes and a pilot, and misses only flaky-test handling and automated contract-compatibility checks.
